title: GDScript doesn't keep native `RefCounted` alive during the call on its method
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible: master

### System information

Godot v4.8.dev (457470a) - EndeavourOS #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Tue, 28 Jul 2026 13:49:51 +0000 on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - Mesa Intel(R) UHD Graphics 630 (CFL GT2) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-9300H CPU @ 2.40GHz (8 threads) - 15.49 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

While testing how https://redirect.github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/117850#issuecomment-4136806530 works in the current master, it occured to me that there is actually nothing preventing `heap-use-after-free` when using native classes, like GDExtension for example.

So, the comment:
> The SomeParent class in my example could presumably just as well be from a GDExtension, and I assume the crash would happen in that scenario too. However we feel about what the contract should be in this case, the current behavior might be well-established enough that this is too breaking of a change.

not just would happen, it already happens when the same situation is recreated.

It will just be very rare, because GDScript VM keeps temporaries alive... I think, not fully sure. From `GDScriptByteCodeGenerator::pop_temporary`
```c++
		// Avoid keeping in the stack long-lived references to objects,
		// which may prevent `RefCounted` objects from being freed.
		// However, the cleanup will be performed an the end of the
		// statement, to allow object references to survive chaining.
```

So the current `RefCounted` behaviour is different when using GDScript classes and native classes.

### Steps to reproduce

Create a native `RefCounted` class that will remove its own last reference during the call from GDScript.

<details>
<summary>GDScript code</summary>

```GDScript
class_name OuterTestGDExt extends Node

var to_remove: InnerGDExt

func _ready() -> void:
    var make_temp: Node = self

    print("call on temp")
    to_remove = InnerGDExt.new()
    to_remove.get_temp(self)
    prints(make_temp.to_remove.test_kept_alive())
    print(to_remove)
    print("-------")
    
    print("get on temp")
    to_remove = InnerGDExt.new()
    to_remove.get_temp(self)
    var _a = make_temp.to_remove.state
    print(to_remove)
    print("-------")
    
    print("set on temp")
    to_remove = InnerGDExt.new()
    to_remove.get_temp(self)
    make_temp.to_remove.state = 100
    print(to_remove)
    print("-------")

    print("call direct")
    to_remove = InnerGDExt.new()
    to_remove.get_temp(self)
    prints("count", to_remove.test_kept_alive())
    print(to_remove)
    print("-------")
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>GDExt code</summary>

```c++
class InnerGDExt : public RefCounted {
	GDCLASS(InnerGDExt, RefCounted)

private:
	Node *outer = nullptr;
	int some_state = 0;

protected:
	static void _bind_methods() {
		ClassDB::bind_method(D_METHOD("test_kept_alive"), &InnerGDExt::test_kept_alive);
		ClassDB::bind_method(D_METHOD("get_state"), &InnerGDExt::get_state);
		ClassDB::bind_method(D_METHOD("set_state", "state"), &InnerGDExt::set_state);
		ClassDB::bind_method(D_METHOD("get_temp", "outer"), &InnerGDExt::get_temp);

		ADD_PROPERTY(PropertyInfo(Variant::INT, "state"), "set_state", "get_state");
	}

public:
	InnerGDExt() {}
	~InnerGDExt() {}
	int test_kept_alive() {
		outer->set("to_remove", nullptr);
		some_state++;
		return get_reference_count();
	}

	int get_state() {
		if (outer) {
			outer->set("to_remove", nullptr);
		}
		some_state++;
		return some_state;
	}
	void set_state(int p_state) {
		if (outer) {
			outer->set("to_remove", nullptr);
		}
		some_state = p_state;
	}
	Ref<InnerGDExt> get_temp(Node *p_outer) {
		outer = p_outer;
		return Ref<InnerGDExt>(this);
	}
};
```
</details>
